precepts.text: Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned. Some are very light because they mixed with Esau, some that did not mix are very dark. Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knoweth it not. Gray hairs are here and there upon him: Ephraim grows old and does not know his own history.
precepts.point: The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors: what God promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob was not yet fulfilled in their day, but Joseph ruled all Egypt. Canaan wasn't ours yet, and Joseph already had the crown.
precepts.why:
“Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned.” Some like to say that is not talking about mixing with other races. It is, and 1 Esdras 8:70 is the precept for it.

Ephraim today is like that: some are very light, extremely light, some able to pass for Esau, because they mixed with Esau; others who did not mix are very dark.

“Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knoweth it not”: the white man has devoured Ephraim's strength, and Ephraim does not realize it. “yea, gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not”: Ephraim grows old and does not know his own history. The fruitful bough of Genesis 49, blessed above his brethren, has been mixed and devoured and has forgotten who he is.

precepts.text: Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart: I will bring them down as the fowls of the heaven. The fowls of the air also refer to man. Imagine those of the circumcision hearing Peter refer to Hosea: remember, he called us fowls. That is why the scripture says prove all things: everything must be proven as it is written, that thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and overcome when thou art judged.
precepts.point: Now the scriptures substantiate the vision Peter had. The vessel knit at the four corners is Israel, and the beasts within it are men. This is why the nations cannot handle us right now: when we speak, we can use the Bible to explain itself. When they hear it, they think it is everybody. No: God said Israel was the vessel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The last creatures in the vessel are the “fowls of the air.” There had to be scripture to show that the fowls of the air also refer to man. Hosea says: “Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria. When they shall go, I will spread my net upon them; I will bring them down as the fowls of the heaven; I will chastise them, as their congregation hath heard.”

Ephraim, the northern kingdom, is the silly dove, brought down as the fowls of the heaven. So the fowls in Peter's vision are Israelites too.

Now imagine those of the circumcision hearing Peter speak: listen, over here in Hosea, remember, God called us fowls. God was showing him it was time to gather the twelve tribes, north and south, back together.

That is why the scripture says prove all things. Everything must be proven as it is written, that thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and overcome when thou art judged. Peter did not just tell a vision; he could prove every creature in it from the prophets.

precepts.text: Ephraim, as I saw Tyrus, is planted in a pleasant place, that island of Puerto Rico, but shall bring forth his children to the murderer; a miscarrying womb and dry breasts. Light or dark, the Lord knows exactly who the northern kingdom is and made sure the seed continued.
precepts.point: Ephraim hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned. Like a pancake, white on top and brown underneath. The whitening campaigns were strategic, to make us forget our heritage.
precepts.why:
“Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned.” Think of a pancake: the top is white and the bottom is brown. We still have that, but you have a lot of light skin, and it was strategic. The whitening campaigns across Latin America were a war on blackness, meant to make us forget our heritage: grandmothers praising good hair and light babies, textbooks erasing black heroes, children taught not to embrace their nose, their lips or their skin. That is how you colonize a people from the inside out. This devil is very evil and very strategic, but there is a God.

“Ephraim, as I saw Tyrus, is planted in a pleasant place: but Ephraim shall bring forth his children to the murderer.” The pleasant place is the island of Puerto Rico. Ephraim and Manasseh are Joseph. “Give them, O Lord: what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.”

A lot of misinformed and uneducated people think the northern kingdom is not Israel just because they are light-skinned. No. The Lord knows exactly who they are, and the Lord made sure the seed would continue. It doesn't matter if they are light or dark; the Lord knows who is who, just as he knew that Asher would land in Brazil, and Brazil is Hebrew for iron. The Lord didn't make a mistake.

So the cake not turned is still Ephraim. Mixed among the people and whitened on top, brought forth to the murderer in a pleasant place, the northern kingdom is still the children of Israel, and the curses on them prove it.

precepts.text: The holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land.
precepts.point: The holy seed was mingled with the strange people of the land. Northern kingdom should learn its own history with the same zeal as the south's.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people”, sometimes willingly, sometimes not. You have knuckleheads who say that is only talking about their customs. It was biological and it was symbolic, dummy. The Bible defines the Bible, and Ezra shows what mixing means: “The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles.”

We did not put away the strange people from the land. We sought after them, because of the ideology of whitening, of bettering the race. The pollutions of the Gentiles are their idolatry and their doctrines, and we became corrupt in our merchandise and commerce. All Israel had that propensity, but here the focus is the northern kingdom.

Read on: “For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land.” When it says mixed himself among the people, it means the seed gets mixed. What is the seed? Sperm, semen. So when somebody comes to you with that BS, this is the scripture to put there: mixing means mixing.

It goes on: “and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.” All of us partook of that, and it is a sin to mix with the other nations. That is why Ephraim is a cake not turned: light on one side and dark on the other, all the different shades among the northern kingdom, and some of our own people with blonde hair and blue eyes whose father is Israel.

precepts.text: They were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.
precepts.point: The holy seed was mingled with the strange people of the land. Northern kingdom should learn its own history with the same zeal as the south's.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people.” Ezra already showed that the holy seed was mixed with the strange people of the land. David gives the other side of it: “But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.” It was not just ideological, dummies, and some of the ones saying it went to seminary school and call themselves theologians. When you look up the definition of mingled, it goes into mixing, just like First Esdras. And they learned their works too.

So Hosea is talking about ideology, and it is also talking about the seed, like we just proved. Scholars know the whitening was both ideological and biological. “Ephraim is a cake not turned. Strangers have devoured his strength.” The cake not turned is the colours, light and dark: some of us light, some in between, some dark.

The strangers devoured more than the strength of the royal seed. Our strength lies in the Lord, the joy of the Lord is our strength, and the ideology cut us away from him. We cannot fight the United States; our countries cannot do any of that. It is time we come back to God. Strangers devoured his strength, “and he knoweth it not: yea, gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not.” Many of our older people are not hearing it; the gray hairs are upon them and they cannot accept it.

And this goes with Matthew 13 and Amos 9, especially for you northern kingdom brothers. Southern kingdom, learn northern kingdom history with the same vigour and zeal that we learn yours. If you are a fisher of men, you fish all the different kinds of fish that pertain to Israel and Christ.

precepts.text: Mine heritage is unto me as a speckled bird.
precepts.point: The holy seed was mingled with the strange people of the land. Northern kingdom should learn its own history with the same zeal as the south's.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Ephraim mixed himself among the people and became “a cake not turned”, light and dark. Jeremiah shows how the Lord sees that mixed people: “Mine heritage is unto me as a speckled bird, the birds round about are against her; come ye, assemble all the beasts of the field, come to devour.”

We are a speckled bird, and the birds round about against her are the enemy. They know who we are because of the caste system. Though we are mixed, they know who we are. In Panama they call the light-skinned ones one name and the darker ones, some of whom are Benjamin, another, and the lady at the hotel sized each of us up by our shade the same way.

But the Lord had a way to fix that, because the Israelite seed is that strong: go back to the Israelite line, and it does not matter how mixed the daughter was. And Hosea says Ephraim would “bring forth his children to the murderer”: Cain, Esau, Edom, the Spaniards, the United States. For those who willingly tried to whiten the race: “give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.” Many of those babies died.

So the speckled bird is still his heritage. “How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel?” Though he struck us with these curses, he will not make us as Admah and Zeboim, the cities round about Sodom and Gomorrah that were utterly destroyed. Our job is to give the word, go to the chief places where our people resort, and let God do the separating.

precepts.text: Woe unto them, for they have fled from me; they have not cried unto me with their heart when they howled upon their beds.
precepts.point: Hosea shows the wandering of the blind: we fled from the Most High, we return but not to the Most High, and the end of it is derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart: And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness”. Hosea shows the wandering of the blind. “When they shall go, I will spread my net upon them; I will bring them down as the fowls of the heaven; I will chastise them, as their congregation hath heard.” Then: “Woe unto them! for they have fled from me: destruction unto them! because they have transgressed against me: though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against me.”

We fled from the Most High. He redeemed us, and we spoke lies against him. “And they have not cried unto me with their heart, when they howled upon their beds: they assemble themselves for corn and wine, and they rebel against me.” Even in our howling we do not cry to him with our heart; we gather for corn and wine, for what we can get, and go on rebelling. That is groping at noonday, and it is why “thou shalt not prosper in thy ways”.

precepts.text: They return, but not to the most High; this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity.
precepts.point: Hosea shows the wandering of the blind: we fled from the Most High, we return but not to the Most High, and the end of it is derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“They return, but not to the most High: they are like a deceitful bow: their princes shall fall by the sword for the rage of their tongue: this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt.” The blind grope and wander. They return, but not to the Most High, like a deceitful bow that does not shoot where it is aimed.

And the end of it is derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity. That is Deuteronomy 28:29: “thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee”: going back into bondage.

precepts.text: Israel mixed among the people is the same speckled heritage, one people made of many shades.
precepts.point: There are many different shades to the Israelites. Israelites come in all shapes, sizes and colors, and a color does not equal a nationality. Your skin tone does not make you a nationality; what the Most High is saying is that the skin tones vary among Israel.

note.label: Jeremiah 12: Why Do the Wicked Prosper

precepts.why:
The Most High calls his heritage “a speckled bird”, with “the birds round about” against her. Hosea shows why Israel is speckled: “Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned.” Israel mixed among the people, and so the heritage came out speckled, one people made of many shades.

That is why there are many different shades to the Israelites. Israelites come in all shapes, sizes and colors, and a color does not equal a nationality. Your skin tone does not make you a nationality; the skin tones vary among Israel, and the speckled bird is still the dearly beloved of his soul, given into the hand of her enemies with all the other birds against her.
